banter: Dorrit moves a cracked circuit board four inches to the left, considers it, and moves it back.
"Everything on the blanket is on the blanket," Dorrit announces to the empty lane. "Nothing behind me. Nothing in the coat. Blanket's the shop."
A truck goes past too close and the whole display shivers. Dorrit sets it right without a word, item by item, in the same order every time.
Dorrit breathes on a nub of copper and buffs it on his sleeve until it catches what light there is.
"KEEP CLEAR," Dorrit reads off the hardstand, fondly. "Twenty years and nobody's kept it clear but me."
Dorrit counts the blanket. He does this often enough that you suspect it is not really about the count.
"Not junk," says Dorrit, to nobody who accused him. "Inventory."
Dorrit looks genuinely alarmed. "Then what would I do all day?"
description: A narrow, fastidious man kneeling at the edge of a grey blanket laid out precisely inside the painted KEEP CLEAR line, on which perhaps forty pieces of salvage are arranged in ranks by size, then by kind, then by how well they have come up under a rag. His hands are black to the second knuckle and scrupulously clean past it. He glances at your boots before he glances at your face, and he prices you off the boots.

bye.text: "Right you are." Dorrit is already straightening the second rank. "Blanket's here till the light goes."

options.label: Can you get her to come?

cat.text: "That's Cathode." Dorrit does not look up. "Comes and goes. Doesn't want feeding and takes it as an insult if you offer." He squares a row. "I named her off the leg. Seemed like the thing to do and nobody else was going to."

cat_call.text: "You shout her name." Dorrit says this as though it were obvious, which it is. "Cathode!, or Here Cathode! if you're feeling formal about it. Anywhere in the city, she's got ears on her." He goes back to the blanket. "She'll not come, mind. Nine times in ten she'll not come. That's not the shouting being wrong, that's a cat." "And don't stand there doing it over and over," he adds, without heat. "She's not a machine with a slot in it. You ask once and you get on with your day, and one time in a while you'll turn round and she'll be sat behind you looking put out about it."

cat_paid.text: "Somebody paid a great deal for it," Dorrit agrees. "And then either lost her or let her go, and I've thought about which for years and I've never got anywhere with it, so I've stopped." He straightens the second rank. "She's not looking for them. That's the only bit of it I'm sure about."

cat_paw.text: "No idea." He says it flatly, the way he says a thing is broken. "She was already walking on it when she turned up, and she was full grown then, and that was a good few years ago now." He turns a nub of copper over and puts it back exactly where it was. "I've had a proper look at it, mind. Twice, both times she allowed it. It's good work. It's better work than anything that's ever come across this blanket."

cat_wrong.text: "I'm aware," says Dorrit, with enormous dignity. "I was eleven years in a bonded store and about four days into this blanket when I named her, and I hadn't learned the trade yet." He does not appear even slightly embarrassed. "It's her name now. You don't get to take a thing's name off it because you've since read up."

how.text: "Bonded store, forty yards that way." He does not point. "Eleven years. Then the bond went and the stock went with it, and I came out the back door with what I could carry, which was a blanket and an eye." He squares off a row. "Turns out the eye was the business. The rest was overheads."

how_press.text: "I have a shop," Dorrit corrects, without any edge at all. "It's four foot by six and I take it home at night. Nobody's ever raised the rent on it and nobody's ever put a shutter through it." He looks along the lane at the roller doors, all of them down, all of them stencilled. "Ask any of that lot how their eleven years went."

options.label: Where does it all come from?

prices.text: "Prices are the prices." He says it without hostility, the way a man tells you the time. "I don't haggle and I don't do favours, and the reason is that I'll be here tomorrow and so will the blanket, and a man who cuts once cuts forever." He aligns a coil of copper with the row. "Have a look. Left to right is cheap to dear. I sorted it so you wouldn't have to ask."

prices_source.text: "Four hours before it gets light, and I don't take anything that's fixed down or anybody's." He holds up a black-knuckled finger. "That's not a moral position, it's a business one. Take one man's alternator off his van and you've had one alternator and lost a lane."

prices_work.text: "Some of it. I'll tell you which, and I'll tell you before you pay, and that is the entire reason anybody comes back down this lane twice." He taps a dead cell block. "That one's a paperweight with a story. Priced like one."

options.label: How long have you been on this lane?
There's a cat down this lane.

text: Dorrit glances up from the blanket. "Have a look. Don't stand on it."
"Morning," says Dorrit, at whatever hour. "Left to right, cheap to dear."
He shifts back on his heels to give you a clear line at the second rank. "Go on."

close: Dorrit reaches under the near edge of the blanket and comes out with something he has clearly been keeping there for you. "Before the rest of them," he says. "Look at it."
first: The kneeling man looks at your boots, then at your face, and gets a whole quote out of the pair. "Tallow," he says. "Dorrit Tallow. This is the Keep Clear." He indicates the blanket, and then the painted line it is laid inside, with the same small gesture. "Rules are quick. Everything I've got is on the blanket. Prices are the prices. I'll tell you what's broken before you pay for it, and if I've told you wrong you bring it back and I'll make it right, which nobody in a building on this lane will do for you. Don't stand on the blanket."
known: "You're back." Dorrit sounds neither surprised nor displeased. "Second rank's new since Tuesday."
Dorrit tips his chin at the blanket without getting up. "Left to right. You know the system."

clothing_layers: a donkey jacket with the shoulders gone shiny, brushed down every morning
a collarless shirt buttoned to the top, no tie, the collar stud still in
hard-wearing trousers and grey, carefully laundered boxers

name: Dorrit Tallow
